source.text: וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵה֖וּד מֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And added [the] sons of Israel to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and Ehud had died.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel again did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and Ehud had died.
en.B: After Ehud had died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} again did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: After Ehud died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} once again did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya tena maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye Ehudi alikuwa amekufa.
sw.B: Ehudi alipokwisha kufa, Waisraeli walifanya tena maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Ehudi alipokufa, Waisraeli walifanya tena yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema ni maovu.

es.L: Y volvieron los hijos de Israel a hacer lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y Aod había muerto.
es.B: Después de que murió Aod, los israelitas volvieron a hacer lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Después de que murió Aod, los israelitas volvieron a hacer lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que era malo.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent encore le mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et Éhoud était mort.
fr.B: Après la mort d’Éhoud, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent encore ce qui est mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Après la mort d’Éhoud, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait une fois encore ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déclarait mauvais.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, khi Ê-hút đã qua đời.
vi.B: Sau khi Ê-hút qua đời, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Sau khi Ê-hút qua đời, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho là ác.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈에 악한 일을 했다. 에훗은 죽었다.
ko.B: 에훗이 죽은 뒤에 이스라엘 백성은 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 보시기에 악한 일을 했다.
ko.R: 에훗이 죽은 뒤에 이스라엘 백성은 또다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 악하다고 하신 일을 했다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel voltaram a fazer o mal aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e Eúde tinha morrido.
pt.B: Depois que Eúde morreu, os israelitas voltaram a fazer o que era mau aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Depois que Eúde morreu, os israelitas mais uma vez fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} considerava mau.

am.L: የእስራኤልም ልጆች {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ዓይን ክፉ የሆነውን ደግመው አደረጉ፤ ናዖድም ሞቶ ነበር።
am.B: ናዖድ ከሞተ በኋላ የእስራኤል ልጆች እንደ ገና {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ክፉ የሆነውን አደረጉ።
am.R: ናዖድ ከሞተ በኋላ እስራኤላውያን እንደ ገና {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ክፉ ነው የሚለውን አደረጉ።

decisions.choice: added to do: did again, went back to doing
decisions.reason: The verb "add" with another verb means doing something once more. Israel returns to the wrongdoing of 3:12, as the cycle of 2:11-19 said it would.

decisions.choice: and Ehud had died: background to the main event, and its cause
decisions.reason: The clause puts the name first and uses a completed verb, which sets the scene rather than moving the story on. The point is that while the judge lived the people held back, and when he died they turned away again, as 2:19 describes. Shamgar (3:31) is not counted here, so this links back to Ehud's eighty years of peace (3:30).

decisions.choice: the evil in the eyes of the LORD: what he judges to be wrong
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means "in the judgment of". The evil is named in 2:11-13 and 3:7: serving other gods.

decisions.choice: After Ehud had died, ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the background clause first, so the reader sees at once why Israel went back to its old ways.

source.text: וַיִּמְכְּרֵ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה בְּיַד֙ יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־כְּנַ֔עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלַ֖ךְ בְּחָצ֑וֹר וְשַׂר־צְבָאוֹ֙ סִֽיסְרָ֔א וְה֥וּא יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בַּחֲרֹ֥שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sold them Yahweh into [the] hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and [the] commander of his army [was] Sisera, and he [was] living in Harosheth-hagoyim.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sold them into [the] hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and the commander of his army [was] Sisera, and he [was] living in Harosheth-hagoyim.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sold them into the power of Jabin, king of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to Jabin, a king of Canaan who ruled from the city of Hazor. The commander of Jabin's army was Sisera. Sisera lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawauza mkononi mwa Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani, aliyetawala huko Hazori; na mkuu wa jeshi lake [alikuwa] Sisera, naye [alikuwa] akikaa Harosheth-hagoyimu.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwauza mikononi mwa Yabini, mfalme wa Kanaani, aliyetawala huko Hazori. Mkuu wa jeshi lake alikuwa Sisera, aliyekaa Harosheth-hagoyimu.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia mikononi mwa Yabini, mfalme mmoja wa Kanaani aliyetawala kutoka mji wa Hazori. Mkuu wa jeshi la Yabini alikuwa Sisera. Sisera aliishi Harosheth-hagoyimu.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los vendió en mano de Jabín, rey de Canaán, que reinaba en Hazor; y el jefe de su ejército [era] Sísara, y él habitaba en Haroset-goyim.
es.B: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los vendió en poder de Jabín, rey de Canaán, que reinaba en Hazor. El jefe de su ejército era Sísara, que vivía en Haroset-goyim.
es.R: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó a Jabín, un rey de Canaán que gobernaba desde la ciudad de Hazor. El jefe del ejército de Jabín era Sísara. Sísara vivía en Haroset-goyim.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les vendit dans la main de Jabin, roi de Canaan, qui régnait à Hatsor ; et le chef de son armée [était] Sisera, et il habitait à Harosheth-Goïm.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les vendit au pouvoir de Jabin, roi de Canaan, qui régnait à Hatsor. Le chef de son armée était Sisera, qui habitait à Harosheth-Goïm.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a livrés à Jabin, un roi de Canaan qui régnait depuis la ville de Hatsor. Le chef de l’armée de Jabin s’appelait Sisera. Sisera habitait à Harosheth-Goïm.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bán họ vào tay Gia-bin, vua Ca-na-an, là vua trị vì tại Hát-so; và tướng chỉ huy quân đội của vua [là] Si-sê-ra, và ông ta [sống] tại Ha-rô-sết Ha-gô-im.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bán họ vào tay Gia-bin, vua Ca-na-an, trị vì tại Hát-so. Tướng chỉ huy quân đội của vua là Si-sê-ra, sống tại Ha-rô-sết Ha-gô-im.
vi.R: Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giao họ cho Gia-bin, một vua Ca-na-an cai trị từ thành Hát-so. Tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Gia-bin là Si-sê-ra. Si-sê-ra sống tại Ha-rô-sết Ha-gô-im.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 하솔에서 다스리는 가나안 왕 야빈의 손에 파셨다. 그의 군대 사령관은 시스라[였고], 그는 하로셋학고임에 살고 [있었다].
ko.B: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들을 하솔에서 다스리는 가나안 왕 야빈의 손에 파셨다. 야빈의 군대 사령관은 시스라였는데, 그는 하로셋학고임에 살았다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들을 가나안의 왕 야빈에게 넘기셨다. 야빈은 하솔 성에서 다스렸다. 야빈의 군대 사령관은 시스라였다. 시스라는 하로셋학고임에 살았다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os vendeu na mão de Jabim, rei de Canaã, que reinava em Hazor; e o comandante do seu exército [era] Sísera, e ele morava em Harosete-Hagoim.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os vendeu ao poder de Jabim, rei de Canaã, que reinava em Hazor. O comandante do seu exército era Sísera, que morava em Harosete-Hagoim.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou a Jabim, um rei de Canaã que governava na cidade de Hazor. O comandante do exército de Jabim era Sísera. Sísera morava em Harosete-Hagoim.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም በከነዓን ንጉሥ በኢያቢስ እጅ ሸጣቸው፤ እርሱም በአሶር ይነግሥ ነበር፤ የሠራዊቱም አለቃ ሲሣራ [ነበረ]፤ እርሱም በሐሮሼት ሐጎይም ይኖር [ነበር]።
am.B: ስለዚህ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በአሶር ይገዛ በነበረው በከነዓን ንጉሥ በኢያቢስ እጅ ሸጣቸው። የሠራዊቱ አለቃ በሐሮሼት ሐጎይም የሚኖረው ሲሣራ ነበረ።
am.R: ስለዚህ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከአሶር ከተማ ይገዛ ለነበረው ለከነዓን ንጉሥ ለኢያቢስ አሳልፎ ሰጣቸው። የኢያቢስ ሠራዊት አለቃ ሲሣራ ነበረ። ሲሣራ የሚኖረው በሐሮሼት ሐጎይም ነበር።

decisions.choice: sold them into the hand of: handed them over to the power of an enemy
decisions.reason: The same picture is used in 2:14, 3:8 and 10:7. God gives his people over to their enemies as one gives up goods in a sale; "hand" means power or control.

decisions.choice: Jabin king of Canaan, reigning in Hazor
decisions.reason: Hazor was the great Canaanite city of the north, above the Sea of Galilee. Joshua 11:1-13 tells of an earlier Jabin of Hazor whom Joshua defeated and whose city he burned; the name may have been used by more than one king of the city. "King of Canaan" calls him ruler of the Canaanites of the region, a stronger title than "king of Hazor".

decisions.choice: Harosheth-hagoyim: a place whose name means "Harosheth of the nations"
decisions.reason: The site is not known for certain. "Of the nations" suggests a district where non-Israelite peoples lived, perhaps in the plain near the Kishon (verse 13). Sisera, whose name is not a Hebrew one, ran Jabin's army from there.

decisions.choice: into the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means power. Balanced keeps the verb "sold" so the reader hears the picture of 2:14, and says "power" so the sense is clear.

decisions.choice: handed them over to
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "sold ... into the hand of" in plain words.

decisions.choice: "Jabín", "Hazor", "Sísara", "Haroset-goyim"; later "Débora", "Lapidot", "Barac hijo de Abinoam", "Cedes", "el monte Tabor", "el Cisón", "Héber el quenita", "Hobab", "Zaanaim", "Jael"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges: names follow the forms long used in Spanish Bibles, as the terms note for these books sets ("Débora", "Barac", "Sísara", "Jael"). "Barac" is also the form of Hebrews 11:32 in this translation.

decisions.choice: "Jabin", "Hatsor", "Sisera", "Harosheth-Goïm"; in this chapter also "Débora", "Lappidoth", "Barak fils d'Abinoam", "Kédesh-Nephtali", "le mont Thabor", "le Kison", "Héber le Kénien", "Hobab", "Tsaanannim", "Yaël"
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10: names follow the terms note ("Débora", "Sisera", "Yaël") and the usual French forms where they exist ("Jabin", "le mont Thabor", "le Kison", as in the Pentateuch drafts); the rest transcribe the Hebrew as elsewhere in these chapters ("Hatsor", with "ts" for tsade).

decisions.choice: the names in this chapter: "Gia-bin", "Hát-so", "Si-sê-ra", "Ha-rô-sết Ha-gô-im", "Đê-bô-ra", "Láp-bi-đốt", "Ba-rác", "A-bi-nô-am", "Kê-đe", "Tha-bô", "Ki-sôn", "Hê-be", "Hô-báp", "Gia-ên"
decisions.reason: Names follow the Protestant transliterations and the terms note for these books; "Ba-rác" is the form of the Vietnamese Hebrews 11:32.

decisions.choice: Jabim, rei de Canaã; Hazor; Sísera; Harosete-Hagoim
decisions.reason: For the whole book (chapters 4-5): the Brazilian forms of the names, "Hazor" as Joshua 11-12 has it in Portuguese; "Sísera" takes the accent that shows its stress on the first syllable. Harosheth-hagoyim (m3) is written as one name with a hyphen, like the compound names of Joshua.

decisions.choice: Jabin is "ኢያቢስ" and Sisera "ሲሣራ" (the terms list for Joshua to Samuel), Hazor "አሶር", Harosheth-hagoyim "ሐሮሼት ሐጎይም". The commander of the army is "የሠራዊቱ አለቃ".
decisions.reason: The names keep the forms Amharic readers know; the place name is left as a name, and its meaning is in the meaning decision.

source.text: וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֠י תְּשַׁ֨ע מֵא֤וֹת רֶֽכֶב־בַּרְזֶל֙ ל֔וֹ וְ֠הוּא לָחַ֞ץ אֶת־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּחָזְקָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, for 900 chariots of iron [were] to him, and he oppressed [the] sons of Israel with force twenty years.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for he had 900 chariots of iron, and he oppressed the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel with force [for] twenty years.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because Jabin had 900 iron chariots and had oppressed the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} harshly for twenty years.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. Jabin had 900 chariots made with iron, and for twenty years he had treated the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cruelly.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana alikuwa na magari ya chuma mia tisa, naye akawaonea wana wa Israeli kwa nguvu [kwa] miaka ishirini.
sw.B: Waisraeli walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu Yabini alikuwa na magari ya vita ya chuma mia tisa, naye alikuwa amewaonea Waisraeli vikali kwa miaka ishirini.
sw.R: Waisraeli walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie. Yabini alikuwa na magari ya vita mia tisa yaliyotengenezwa kwa chuma, naye alikuwa amewatesa Waisraeli kwa ukatili kwa miaka ishirini.

es.L: Y clamaron los hijos de Israel {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque él tenía novecientos carros de hierro, y oprimió con dureza a los hijos de Israel [durante] veinte años.
es.B: Los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque Jabín tenía novecientos carros de hierro y había oprimido con dureza a los israelitas durante veinte años.
es.R: Los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda. Jabín tenía novecientos carros de guerra reforzados con hierro, y durante veinte años había tratado con crueldad a los israelitas.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, car il avait neuf cents chars de fer, et il opprima les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël avec violence [pendant] vingt ans.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, car Jabin avait neuf cents chars de fer et il opprimait durement les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} depuis vingt ans.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont appelé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au secours. Jabin avait neuf cents chars garnis de fer, et depuis vingt ans, il traitait les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} avec cruauté.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì vua có chín trăm xe chiến bằng sắt, và vua đã áp bức con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên cách tàn bạo hai mươi năm.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì Gia-bin có chín trăm xe chiến bằng sắt và đã áp bức dân Y-sơ-ra-ên cách tàn bạo suốt hai mươi năm.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ. Gia-bin có chín trăm xe chiến được bọc sắt, và suốt hai mươi năm vua ấy đã đối xử tàn ác với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. 그에게 철 병거 구백 대가 있었고, 그가 이십 년 동안 이스라엘 자손을 힘으로 억압하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. 야빈에게는 철 병거가 구백 대나 있었고, 그는 이십 년 동안 이스라엘 백성을 혹독하게 억압했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 도와 달라고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. 야빈에게는 쇠로 만든 전차가 구백 대나 있었다. 그리고 그는 이십 년 동안 이스라엘 백성을 몹시 괴롭혔다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, porque ele tinha novecentos carros de ferro, e ele oprimiu os filhos de Israel com violência [durante] vinte anos.
pt.B: Os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, porque Jabim tinha novecentos carros de ferro e havia vinte anos que oprimia duramente os israelitas.
pt.R: Os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} pedindo ajuda. Jabim tinha novecentos carros de guerra reforçados com ferro, e havia vinte anos que tratava os israelitas com crueldade.

am.L: የእስራኤልም ልጆች {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጮኹ፤ እርሱ 900 የብረት ሰረገሎች ነበሩትና፤ የእስራኤልንም ልጆች [ለ]ሃያ ዓመት በኃይል አስጨንቋቸው ነበርና።
am.B: የእስራኤል ልጆች {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጮኹ፤ ኢያቢስ 900 የብረት ሰረገሎች ነበሩት፤ የእስራኤልንም ልጆች ለሃያ ዓመት አጥብቆ ጨቁኗቸው ነበርና።
am.R: እስራኤላውያን እንዲረዳቸው {{divine_name:ወደ እግዚአብሔር|ወደ ያህዌ}} ጮኹ። ኢያቢስ በብረት የተለበጡ 900 ሰረገሎች ነበሩት፤ ለሃያ ዓመትም እስራኤላውያንን በጭካኔ ሲያሠቃያቸው ቆይቷል።

decisions.choice: chariots of iron: war chariots fitted with iron parts
decisions.reason: Chariots were built of wood and leather; "iron" most likely refers to iron fittings, such as tires, axles or plates, that made them strong. In the open plains they gave the Canaanites an army Israel's foot soldiers could not face (1:19; Joshua 17:16-18).

decisions.choice: for: the reason Israel cried out
decisions.reason: The clause explains the cry. Twenty years under a ruler with such a chariot force left Israel no way to free itself.

decisions.choice: oppressed with force: crushed them harshly
decisions.reason: The verb means to press or squeeze, and "with force" stresses how hard the rule was. The same verb is used of Israel's oppressors in 2:18.

decisions.choice: cried out ... for help
decisions.reason: The cry is a call for rescue, as in 3:9 and 3:15. Readable adds "for help" to make that plain.

decisions.choice: Jabin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he". Balanced and Readable name Jabin, so the pronoun is not taken to mean the LORD.

source.text: וּדְבוֹרָה֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה נְבִיאָ֔ה אֵ֖שֶׁת לַפִּיד֑וֹת הִ֛יא שֹׁפְטָ֥ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא׃

en.L: And Deborah, a woman, a prophetess, wife of Lappidoth, she [was] judging Israel at that time.
en.B: Now Deborah, a prophet, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
en.R: At that time a woman named Deborah was leading Israel. She was a prophet, and she was the wife of Lappidoth.

sw.L: Naye Debora, mwanamke, nabii, mke wa Lapidothi, yeye [alikuwa] akiwaamua Israeli wakati ule.

es.R: En aquel tiempo una mujer llamada Débora dirigía a Israel. Era profetisa y era la esposa de Lapidot.

fr.B: Or Débora, une prophétesse, la femme de Lappidoth, jugeait Israël en ce temps-là.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, c’était une femme, Débora, qui dirigeait Israël. Elle était prophétesse, et elle était la femme de Lappidoth.

vi.L: Và Đê-bô-ra, một người nữ, một nữ tiên tri, vợ của Láp-bi-đốt, bà [đang] xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên vào thời ấy.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đê-bô-ra, một nữ tiên tri, vợ của Láp-bi-đốt, đang xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Vào thời ấy, một người phụ nữ tên là Đê-bô-ra đang lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên. Bà là một nữ tiên tri, và là vợ của Láp-bi-đốt.

ko.L: 그리고 랍비돗의 아내인 여자 예언자 드보라, 그 여자가 그때에 이스라엘을 다스리고 [있었다].
ko.B: 그때 랍비돗의 아내인 예언자 드보라가 이스라엘을 다스리고 있었다.
ko.R: 그때 드보라라는 여자가 이스라엘을 이끌고 있었다. 그는 예언자였고, 랍비돗의 아내였다.

pt.L: E Débora, mulher, profetisa, esposa de Lapidote, ela julgava Israel naquele tempo.
pt.B: Naquele tempo, Débora, uma profetisa, esposa de Lapidote, julgava Israel.
pt.R: Naquele tempo, uma mulher chamada Débora liderava Israel. Ela era profetisa e era esposa de Lapidote.

am.L: ሴት ነቢዪት የሆነችው የለፊዶት ሚስት ዲቦራም፣ እርሷ በዚያን ጊዜ እስራኤልን ትዳኝ ነበር።
am.B: በዚያን ጊዜ የለፊዶት ሚስት ነቢዪቱ ዲቦራ እስራኤልን ትዳኝ ነበር።
am.R: በዚያን ጊዜ ዲቦራ የምትባል ሴት እስራኤልን ትመራ ነበር። እርሷ ነቢዪት ነበረች፤ የለፊዶትም ሚስት ነበረች።

decisions.choice: a woman, a prophetess: a woman who spoke God's word
decisions.reason: The noun is the feminine form of the word for "prophet", used also of Miriam (Exodus 15:20), Huldah (2 Kings 22:14) and Isaiah's wife (Isaiah 8:3). The word "woman" set beside it is emphatic: the story will turn on what a woman does (verse 9). Deborah speaks for God in verses 6-7, 9 and 14.

decisions.choice: wife of Lappidoth: Deborah's husband was named Lappidoth
alternatives: a woman of torches (a fiery woman)
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "wife of Lappidoth", naming her husband, as Hebrew usually does when it introduces a woman. But the word for "wife" also means "woman", and "lappidoth" is the plural of the word for "torch" (used in 7:16 and 15:4). So it may describe her as "a woman of torches", that is, a fiery, spirited woman. The ending of the name is unusual for a man. Some have also linked "torches" with Barak, whose name means "lightning", but nothing in the text says he was her husband. The text gives no other word about a husband, so either reading is possible; this translation follows the usual pattern of an introduction and reads a name.

decisions.choice: judging Israel: leading Israel and settling its disputes
decisions.reason: On "judge" in this book see 2:16: a leader raised to rescue and govern Israel. The form here describes an ongoing role at that time. Deborah's judging included hearing cases (verse 5), and through her the LORD calls Israel to battle (verse 6).

decisions.choice: a prophet
decisions.reason: English now uses "prophet" for women and men alike. "A woman" is not repeated, since "Deborah" and "wife" already make it plain; the meaning decision keeps its emphasis.

decisions.choice: At that time ...
decisions.reason: Readable starts with the time and splits the description into short sentences.

decisions.choice: "nabii" for the prophetess, with "mwanamke" (a woman) beside it at Literal
decisions.reason: Swahili "nabii" serves for a man or a woman, so no feminine form is needed; the Hebrew already says "a woman" before the title, and Literal keeps both words.

decisions.choice: "profetisa" at every level
alternatives: "profeta" (Spanish also uses the masculine form for women)
decisions.reason: Spanish has a feminine form for a woman who speaks God's word (m1), long used for Deborah and Miriam; the English Balanced "a prophet" says the same thing.

decisions.choice: "une prophétesse" at every level
decisions.reason: French has its own feminine noun, "prophétesse", the usual word for a woman who speaks God's word (Miriam, Exodus 15:20). It says nothing less than "prophète"; the English Balanced says "a prophet" because English now uses that word for women too.

decisions.choice: "nữ tiên tri"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks a woman prophet with "nữ"; the English Balanced "a prophet" makes the same point that she spoke God's word (m1).

decisions.choice: Deborah is "bà" in the narrative
decisions.reason: A married woman who leads Israel and judges its disputes is spoken of with respect; "bà" is kept for her through chapters 4 and 5.

decisions.choice: "예언자" for the prophetess, with "여자" (woman) at Literal
decisions.reason: "예언자" is the modern word this translation uses for prophet; Literal keeps the Hebrew's "a woman, a prophetess" with "여자 예언자". Korean "그" serves for her as for a man, as in modern writing.

decisions.choice: Débora, profetisa (every level); Lapidote
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Portuguese has its own feminine "profetisa", the word for Miriam in Exodus 15:20 in Portuguese, so every level uses it where the English Balanced and Readable say "prophet"; it keeps the stress on her being a woman (m1) without repeating "mulher" outside Literal. "Débora" and "Lapidote" are the Brazilian forms of the names.

decisions.choice: "ነቢዪት" (prophetess) at every level; Deborah "እስራኤልን ትዳኝ ነበር" (Literal, Balanced), "ትመራ ነበር" (Readable), as for the other judges.
decisions.reason: Amharic marks the prophet's sex in the word itself, as Exodus 15:20 does for Miriam, so the feminine form is the plain one at every level.

source.text: וְ֠הִיא יוֹשֶׁ֨בֶת תַּֽחַת־תֹּ֜מֶר דְּבוֹרָ֗ה בֵּ֧ין הָרָמָ֛ה וּבֵ֥ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֵלֶ֛יהָ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And she [was] sitting under [the] palm of Deborah, between the Ramah and between Bethel, in [the] hill country of Ephraim; and went up to her [the] sons of Israel for the judgment.

en.L: And she [was] sitting under the palm tree of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel, in the hill country of Ephraim; and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went up to her for judgment.
en.B: She used to hold court under the Palm of Deborah, in the hill country of Ephraim between Ramah and Bethel, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came up to her to have their disputes decided.
en.R: She would sit under a palm tree that was named after her, the Palm of Deborah. It was between the towns of Ramah and Bethel, in the hills of Ephraim. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} would come to her there, and she would settle their disputes.

sw.L: Naye [alikuwa] akiketi chini ya mtende wa Debora, kati ya Rama na Betheli, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu; nao wana wa Israeli wakapanda kwake kwa ajili ya hukumu.
sw.B: Alikuwa akiketi kuamua mashauri chini ya Mtende wa Debora, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu kati ya Rama na Betheli, nao Waisraeli walikwenda kwake ili mashauri yao yaamuliwe.
sw.R: Alikuwa akiketi chini ya mtende ulioitwa kwa jina lake, Mtende wa Debora. Mtende huo ulikuwa kati ya miji ya Rama na Betheli, katika vilima vya Efraimu. Waisraeli walikuwa wakimjia huko, naye aliwamalizia mabishano yao.

es.L: Y ella se sentaba debajo de la palmera de Débora, entre Ramá y Betel, en la región montañosa de Efraín; y los hijos de Israel subían a ella para el juicio.
es.B: Solía sentarse a juzgar bajo la Palmera de Débora, en la región montañosa de Efraín, entre Ramá y Betel, y los israelitas subían a ella para que resolviera sus pleitos.
es.R: Ella se sentaba debajo de una palmera que llevaba su nombre, la Palmera de Débora. Estaba entre las ciudades de Ramá y Betel, en las montañas de Efraín. Los israelitas iban allí a verla, y ella resolvía sus pleitos.

fr.L: Et elle siégeait sous le palmier de Débora, entre Rama et Béthel, dans la montagne d’Éphraïm ; et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël montaient vers elle pour le jugement.
fr.B: Elle siégeait sous le Palmier de Débora, dans la région montagneuse d’Éphraïm, entre Rama et Béthel, et les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} montaient vers elle pour faire juger leurs différends.
fr.R: Elle s’asseyait sous un palmier qui portait son nom, le Palmier de Débora. Il se trouvait entre les villes de Rama et de Béthel, dans les collines d’Éphraïm. Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} venaient la voir là, et elle réglait leurs disputes.

vi.L: Và bà [thường] ngồi dưới cây chà là Đê-bô-ra, giữa Ra-ma và Bê-tên, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im; và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên lên gặp bà để được xét xử.
vi.B: Bà thường ngồi xét xử dưới cây Chà Là Đê-bô-ra, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im, giữa Ra-ma và Bê-tên, và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lên gặp bà để bà phân xử các vụ tranh chấp.
vi.R: Bà thường ngồi dưới một cây chà là được đặt theo tên bà, gọi là cây Chà Là Đê-bô-ra. Cây ấy ở giữa các thành Ra-ma và Bê-tên, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im. Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên thường đến gặp bà ở đó, và bà phân xử các vụ tranh chấp của họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그 여자는 에브라임 산지 라마와 벧엘 사이, 드보라의 종려나무 아래에 앉아 [있었다]. 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 재판을 받으려고 그 여자에게로 올라갔다.
ko.B: 드보라는 에브라임 산지의 라마와 벧엘 사이에 있는 '드보라의 종려나무' 아래에 앉아 재판하곤 했다. 이스라엘 백성은 그에게 올라와서 다툼을 판결받았다.
ko.R: 드보라는 한 종려나무 아래에 앉아 있곤 했다. 그 나무는 그의 이름을 따서 '드보라의 종려나무'라고 불렸다. 그 나무는 에브라임 산지의 라마 성읍과 벧엘 성읍 사이에 있었다. 이스라엘 백성은 그곳으로 드보라를 찾아왔고, 드보라는 그들의 다툼을 해결해 주었다.

pt.L: E ela se sentava debaixo da palmeira de Débora, entre Ramá e Betel, na região montanhosa de Efraim; e os filhos de Israel subiam a ela para o julgamento.
pt.B: Ela costumava atender debaixo da Palmeira de Débora, na região montanhosa de Efraim, entre Ramá e Betel, e os israelitas subiam até ela para que decidisse as suas questões.
pt.R: Ela se sentava debaixo de uma palmeira que tinha o seu nome, a Palmeira de Débora. A árvore ficava entre as cidades de Ramá e Betel, nas montanhas de Efraim. Os israelitas iam até ela ali, e ela resolvia as suas questões.

am.L: እርሷም በኤፍሬም ኮረብታማ አገር በራማና በቤቴል መካከል ባለው በዲቦራ ዘንባባ ዛፍ ሥር ትቀመጥ ነበር፤ የእስራኤልም ልጆች ለፍርድ ወደ እርሷ ይወጡ ነበር።
am.B: በኤፍሬም ኮረብታማ አገር በራማና በቤቴል መካከል የዲቦራ ዘንባባ በተባለው ዛፍ ሥር ተቀምጣ ትፈርድ ነበር፤ የእስራኤል ልጆችም ክርክራቸው እንዲወሰንላቸው ወደ እርሷ ይመጡ ነበር።
am.R: እርሷ በስሟ በተሰየመ፣ የዲቦራ ዘንባባ በሚባል የዘንባባ ዛፍ ሥር ትቀመጥ ነበር። ዛፉም በኤፍሬም ኮረብቶች በራማና በቤቴል ከተሞች መካከል ነበረ። እስራኤላውያንም ወደዚያ ወደ እርሷ ይመጡ ነበር፤ እርሷም ክርክራቸውን ትዳኝላቸው ነበር።

decisions.choice: sitting: what she did regularly
decisions.reason: The form describes a habit: this was where she usually held court, as judges and elders sat to hear cases (Ruth 4:1-2).

decisions.choice: the palm of Deborah: a landmark tree known by her name
decisions.reason: A single tree could serve as a well-known meeting place. Genesis 35:8 names a tree near Bethel after another Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, but the two are different trees and different women.

decisions.choice: for judgment: to have their cases decided
decisions.reason: Here the noun means a legal decision. People came to her to settle disputes they could not settle themselves.

decisions.choice: the Palm of Deborah

records.literal_gloss: And she sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, Has not commanded Yahweh God of Israel: Go and march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousands men from [the] sons of Naphtali and from [the] sons of Zebulun?

en.L: And she sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, "Has not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, commanded, 'Go, and march to Mount Tabor, and take with you 10,000 men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun.
en.B: She sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali. She told him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has given you this command: 'Go, lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take 10,000 men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun with you.
en.R: Deborah sent for a man named Barak, the son of Abinoam. He lived in the town of Kedesh, in the land of the tribe of Naphtali. She said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, is giving you this order: 'Go to Mount Tabor. Take 10,000 men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun with you.

sw.L: Naye akatuma akamwita Baraka mwana wa Abinoamu kutoka Kedesh-naftali, akamwambia, "Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, hajaamuru, 'Nenda, ukajipange kwenye Mlima Tabori, uchukue pamoja nawe watu elfu kumi katika wana wa Naftali na katika wana wa Zabuloni.
sw.B: Alituma mtu kumwita Baraka mwana wa Abinoamu kutoka Kedeshi katika Naftali. Akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, amekuamuru hivi: 'Nenda, uongoze watu mpaka Mlima Tabori, uchukue pamoja nawe watu elfu kumi kutoka makabila ya Naftali na Zabuloni.
sw.R: Debora alimtuma mtu kumwita mtu mmoja aitwaye Baraka, mwana wa Abinoamu. Baraka aliishi katika mji wa Kedeshi, katika nchi ya kabila la Naftali. Debora akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, anakupa agizo hili: 'Nenda Mlima Tabori. Chukua pamoja nawe watu elfu kumi kutoka makabila ya Naftali na Zabuloni.

fr.L: Et elle envoya appeler Barak, fils d’Abinoam, de Kédesh-Nephtali, et elle lui dit : « N’est-ce pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, qui [t’]a ordonné : “Va, et dirige-toi vers le mont Thabor, et prends avec toi dix mille hommes des fils de Nephtali et des fils de Zabulon.

am.L: እርሷም ልካ የአቢኒኤምን ልጅ ባርቅን ከቃዴስ ንፍታሌም ጠራችው፤ እንዲህም አለችው፦ «የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}፦ “ሂድ፤ ወደ ታቦር ተራራም ዝመት፤ ከንፍታሌም ልጆችና ከዛብሎን ልጆች 10,000 ሰዎችን ከአንተ ጋር ውሰድ።
am.B: እርሷም ልካ የአቢኒኤምን ልጅ ባርቅን ከንፍታሌም ምድር ከቃዴስ አስጠራችው። እንዲህም አለችው፦ «የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይህን ትእዛዝ ሰጥቶሃል፦ “ሂድ፤ ከንፍታሌምና ከዛብሎን ነገዶች 10,000 ሰዎችን ይዘህ እየመራህ ወደ ታቦር ተራራ ውጣ።
am.R: ዲቦራ የአቢኒኤምን ልጅ ባርቅን አስጠራችው። እርሱ በንፍታሌም ነገድ ምድር በቃዴስ ከተማ ይኖር ነበር። እርሷም እንዲህ አለችው፦ «የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይህን ትእዛዝ ይሰጥሃል፦ “ወደ ታቦር ተራራ ሂድ። ከንፍታሌምና ከዛብሎን ነገዶች 10,000 ሰዎችን ይዘህ ሂድ።

decisions.choice: Has not the LORD commanded? A question that means "the LORD has commanded"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes". Deborah is not asking for information; she is telling Barak what God has ordered, perhaps as a word he has not yet obeyed.

decisions.choice: march: lead out, draw the men up
decisions.reason: The verb means "draw" or "pull". Here it describes leading troops out or spreading them out in order. The same verb is used in verse 7 of God "drawing" Sisera out, so the two sides are drawn to one place.

decisions.choice: Kedesh-naphtali and Mount Tabor
decisions.reason: Kedesh in Naphtali lay in the north of Galilee (Joshua 19:37; 20:7). Mount Tabor is a steep, round hill at the northeast edge of the Jezreel valley, where the tribes of Zebulun, Naphtali and Issachar met (Joshua 19:12, 22, 34). From its slopes foot soldiers were safe from chariots.

decisions.choice: ten thousand: the number of men called up
decisions.reason: On the size of such numbers see the note at Numbers 1. Here the figure is the force raised from two tribes.

decisions.choice: from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a tribe's ancestor means its members. The men called up are the tribes' fighting men, so Balanced and Readable say "tribes" and need no inclusive wording.

decisions.choice: has given you this command / is giving you this order
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into the statement it implies, and keep God's words as a quotation inside Deborah's.

decisions.choice: "Barak", the form of Hebrews 11:32 in French
alternatives: "Baraq", the form proposed in the terms note
decisions.reason: The terms note says that a name already published in the New Testament wins. Hebrews 11:32 in the French of this translation says "Barak" at every level, so Judges uses the same form.

decisions.choice: Deborah speaks to Barak in the plain style (해라체); Barak answers her in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: Deborah speaks as the judge of Israel and as a prophet bringing God's command, and Barak answers the leader who summoned him. A reviewer may prefer a softer style for Deborah.

decisions.choice: Deborah and Barak speak as "tôi" and "ông" / "bà"
decisions.reason: Deborah speaks for God but to a leader of Israel as an equal in rank; "ông" and "bà" keep the respect each owes the other. The LORD's own words in her mouth keep his forms ("ngươi" at Literal, verse 7).

decisions.choice: você (Deborah to Barak); tu (the LORD to Barak, in the quoted command)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Deborah speaks to Barak with "você", as people speak to each other, and the LORD's command she quotes keeps God's "tu" ("Vai", "toma contigo"), as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets it, so the reader hears whose words are whose. Barak answers her with "você" (verse 8). "Baraque", "Abinoão" and "Quedes" (Joshua 20:7) are the Brazilian forms of the names.

decisions.choice: Literal keeps the question "Has not the LORD commanded ...?", but Amharic puts its verb last: the command is quoted first and the question "ብሎ አላዘዘህምን?" closes it at the end of verse 7.
alternatives: a statement, as at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Amharic cannot open a sentence with "has he not commanded" and then quote the command; the quotation marks stay where the English has them.

decisions.choice: Deborah says "አንተ" to Barak, and Barak "አንቺ" to Deborah (verse 8).
alternatives: "እርስዎ" from Barak to the prophetess who judges Israel
decisions.reason: They speak as fellow leaders of Israel's war, the way the terms list has equals speak; Deborah brings God's word to him, which a prophet does with "አንተ". A reviewer may prefer "እርስዎ" from Barak, given her office.

vi.L: Và Ta sẽ dụ Si-sê-ra, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Gia-bin, cùng các xe chiến và đám quân đông đảo của hắn đến với ngươi tại suối Ki-sôn, và Ta sẽ phó hắn vào tay ngươi'?"
vi.B: Ta sẽ dụ Si-sê-ra, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Gia-bin, cùng các xe chiến và đoàn quân của hắn ra gặp con tại sông Ki-sôn, và Ta sẽ giao hắn vào tay con.'"

ko.L: 그리고 내가 야빈의 군대 사령관 시스라와 그의 병거들과 그의 무리를 기손 시내로 너에게 끌어내어, 그를 네 손에 주겠다.'"
ko.B: 내가 야빈의 군대 사령관 시스라를 그의 병거들과 군대와 함께 기손 강으로 끌어내어 너와 맞서게 하고, 그를 네 손에 넘겨주겠다.'"
ko.R: 내가 야빈의 군대 사령관 시스라를 기손 강으로 이끌어 내어 너와 싸우게 하겠다. 그는 병거들과 군인들을 데리고 올 것이다. 그러나 나는 네가 그를 이기게 하겠다.'"

pt.L: E atrairei a ti, ao ribeiro Quisom, Sísera, o comandante do exército de Jabim, e os seus carros e a sua multidão, e o entregarei na tua mão'?"
pt.B: Eu atrairei Sísera, o comandante do exército de Jabim, com os seus carros e as suas tropas, até o rio Quisom para te enfrentar, e o entregarei nas tuas mãos.'"
pt.R: Eu vou levar Sísera, o comandante do exército de Jabim, até o rio Quisom para lutar contra ti. Ele vai trazer os seus carros de guerra e os seus soldados. Mas eu vou deixar que tu o derrotes.'"

am.L: እኔም የኢያቢስን ሠራዊት አለቃ ሲሣራን ከሰረገሎቹና ከብዙ ሠራዊቱ ጋር ወደ ቂሶን ጅረት ወደ አንተ እስበዋለሁ፤ በእጅህም እሰጠዋለሁ” ብሎ አላዘዘህምን?»

decisions.choice: the wadi Kishon: the stream that drains the Jezreel valley
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream bed that may run dry in summer and flood in the rainy season. The Kishon flows west through the plain below Mount Tabor to the sea near Mount Carmel. The Song of Deborah says it swept the enemy away (5:21).

decisions.choice: I will draw ... I will give him into your hand: God himself brings the enemy and hands him over
decisions.reason: The battle plan is God's. He draws Sisera to the place of his choosing, as he drew Pharaoh out after Israel (Exodus 14:4), and the promise "I will give him into your hand" is the regular word of a victory given by God (1:2; 3:28).

decisions.choice: his multitude: his great mass of troops
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd or noisy throng; with the chariots it means the rest of Sisera's army.

decisions.choice: the Kishon River
decisions.reason: "Wadi" is not a common English word. Balanced and Readable say "river"; the meaning decision explains that it was a seasonal stream.

decisions.choice: I will let you defeat him
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "give him into your hand" in plain words.

decisions.choice: "el torrente Cisón" (L); "el río Cisón" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a stream bed that fills in the rainy season (m1). Literal says "torrente", the Spanish word for such a stream; Balanced and Readable say "río", as the English says "River".

decisions.choice: "le torrent du Kison" at every level
alternatives: "la rivière Kison", as the English "the Kishon River"
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream bed that fills in the rainy season. French "torrent" is the usual word for it, and "le Kison" is the form already used in French; Readable keeps it too, since "torrent" is a common word.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Barak as "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R), with "Ta" for himself
decisions.reason: God speaking to one person who serves him calls him "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable, as the Genesis terms note and the Pentateuch set; God's words to a king or priest he is judging, to Israel as a nation, and to the nations keep "ngươi" / "các ngươi" at every level. Barak is a man God commands to serve him, so the warmer "con" stands at Balanced and Readable; the rebukes to Israel (2:1; 10:11) keep "các ngươi". Deborah herself calls Barak "ông". Recorded once here for the book.

decisions.choice: o ribeiro Quisom (L); o rio Quisom (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 4:13; 5:21): the seasonal stream (m1) is "ribeiro" at Literal, the Portuguese word for a small stream, and "rio" at Balanced and Readable, as the English says "River". "Quisom" is the Brazilian form of the name.

decisions.choice: The wadi Kishon is "የቂሶን ጅረት" (Literal) and "የቂሶን ወንዝ" (Balanced, Readable), here and in 4:13 and 5:21.
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream bed that fills in the rainy season; "ጅረት" (stream) is closer at Literal, and the other levels follow the English "River".

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Barak, If you go with me, and I will go; and if not you go with me, not I will go.

en.L: And Barak said to her, "If you go with me, then I will go; but if you do not go with me, I will not go."
en.B: Barak answered her, "If you go with me, I will go. But if you do not go with me, I will not go."
en.R: Barak answered, "I will go if you go with me. But if you do not go with me, I will not go."

sw.B: Baraka alimjibu, "Ukienda pamoja nami, nitakwenda. Lakini usipokwenda pamoja nami, sitakwenda."

es.B: Barac le respondió: «Si tú vas conmigo, iré. Pero si no vas conmigo, no iré.»
es.R: Barac le respondió: «Iré si tú vas conmigo. Pero si no vas conmigo, no iré.»

fr.B: Barak lui répondit : « Si tu viens avec moi, j’irai. Mais si tu ne viens pas avec moi, je n’irai pas. »
fr.R: Barak a répondu : « J’irai si tu viens avec moi. Mais si tu ne viens pas avec moi, je n’irai pas. »

vi.B: Ba-rác đáp: "Nếu bà đi với tôi, tôi sẽ đi. Nhưng nếu bà không đi với tôi, tôi sẽ không đi."
vi.R: Ba-rác đáp: "Tôi sẽ đi nếu bà đi với tôi. Nhưng nếu bà không đi với tôi, tôi sẽ không đi."

ko.L: 그러자 바락이 그 여자에게 말했다. "당신이 나와 함께 가면 내가 가겠습니다. 그러나 당신이 나와 함께 가지 않으면 나는 가지 않겠습니다."
ko.B: 바락이 드보라에게 대답했다. "함께 가 주시면 가겠습니다. 그러나 함께 가 주지 않으시면 가지 않겠습니다."
ko.R: 바락이 대답했다. "함께 가 주시면 저도 가겠습니다. 그러나 함께 가 주지 않으시면 저는 가지 않겠습니다."

pt.L: E Baraque lhe disse: "Se você for comigo, então eu irei; mas, se você não for comigo, não irei."
pt.B: Baraque lhe respondeu: "Se você for comigo, eu irei. Mas, se você não for comigo, não irei."
pt.R: Baraque respondeu: "Eu vou, se você for comigo. Mas, se você não for comigo, eu não vou."

decisions.choice: two balanced conditions: Barak's going depends on hers
decisions.reason: Barak sets a condition. He does not refuse, but he will not go unless the prophet goes with him. Verse 9 shows that this costs him the honor of the victory.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends with "I will not go"
alternatives: adds: for I do not know the day when the LORD will send his angel to give me success
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text ends here. The early Greek translation adds Barak's reason: that he does not know the day on which the LORD will give success by his angel. That looks like an explanation added later, and the Hebrew is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

source.text: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָלֹ֧ךְ אֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗ךְ אֶ֚פֶס כִּי֩ לֹ֨א תִֽהְיֶ֜ה תִּֽפְאַרְתְּךָ֗ עַל־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה הוֹלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֣י בְֽיַד־אִשָּׁ֔ה יִמְכֹּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־סִֽיסְרָ֑א וַתָּ֧קָם דְּבוֹרָ֛ה וַתֵּ֥לֶךעִם־בָּרָ֖ק קֶֽדְשָׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, Going I will go with you; only that not will be your honor on the way that you [are] going, for into [the] hand of a woman will sell Yahweh Sisera. And arose Deborah and went with Barak to Kedesh.

en.L: And she said, "I will surely go with you; only the honor will not be yours on the way that you are going, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will sell Sisera into [the] hand of a woman." And Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
en.B: "I will certainly go with you," she said. "But on the road you are taking, the honor will not be yours, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will hand Sisera over to a woman." So Deborah set out with Barak for Kedesh.
en.R: "Yes, I will go with you," she said. "But the way you are going, you will not get the honor. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will let a woman defeat Sisera." So Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Hakika nitakwenda pamoja nawe; ila heshima haitakuwa yako katika njia unayoiendea, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamuuza Sisera mkononi mwa mwanamke." Naye Debora akainuka, akaenda pamoja na Baraka mpaka Kedeshi.
sw.B: Akasema, "Hakika nitakwenda pamoja nawe. Lakini katika njia unayoiendea heshima haitakuwa yako, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamtia Sisera mikononi mwa mwanamke." Basi Debora aliondoka akaenda pamoja na Baraka mpaka Kedeshi.
sw.R: Akasema, "Ndiyo, nitakwenda pamoja nawe. Lakini kwa njia unayoichagua, hutapata heshima. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamwezesha mwanamke kumshinda Sisera." Basi Debora alikwenda pamoja na Baraka mpaka Kedeshi.

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Ciertamente iré contigo; solo que no será tuya la honra en el camino por donde vas, porque en mano de una mujer venderá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Sísara.» Y se levantó Débora y fue con Barac a Cedes.
es.B: «Desde luego que iré contigo», dijo ella. «Pero en el camino que emprendes la honra no será tuya, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregará a Sísara en manos de una mujer.» Así que Débora partió con Barac hacia Cedes.
es.R: «Sí, iré contigo», dijo ella. «Pero tal como lo estás haciendo, tú no te llevarás la honra. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará que una mujer derrote a Sísara.» Y Débora fue con Barac a Cedes.

fr.L: Et elle dit : « J’irai sûrement avec toi ; seulement, l’honneur ne sera pas pour toi sur le chemin où tu vas, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vendra Sisera dans la main d’une femme. » Et Débora se leva et alla avec Barak à Kédesh.
fr.B: « Bien sûr, j’irai avec toi, dit-elle. Mais sur le chemin que tu prends, l’honneur ne sera pas pour toi, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} livrera Sisera à une femme. » Débora se mit donc en route avec Barak pour Kédesh.
fr.R: « Oui, j’irai avec toi, a-t-elle dit. Mais de la façon dont tu fais les choses, ce n’est pas toi qui en auras l’honneur. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va donner à une femme la victoire sur Sisera. » Débora est donc partie avec Barak à Kédesh.

vi.L: Và bà nói: "Chắc chắn tôi sẽ đi với ông; chỉ có điều vinh dự sẽ không thuộc về ông trên con đường ông đang đi, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ bán Si-sê-ra vào tay một người nữ." Và Đê-bô-ra đứng dậy và đi với Ba-rác đến Kê-đe.
vi.B: Bà nói: "Chắc chắn tôi sẽ đi với ông. Nhưng trên con đường ông đang đi, vinh dự sẽ không thuộc về ông, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ giao Si-sê-ra vào tay một người phụ nữ." Vậy Đê-bô-ra lên đường đi với Ba-rác đến Kê-đe.
vi.R: Bà nói: "Được, tôi sẽ đi với ông. Nhưng theo cách ông đang làm, ông sẽ không được vinh dự. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ để một người phụ nữ đánh bại Si-sê-ra." Vậy Đê-bô-ra đi với Ba-rác đến Kê-đe.

ko.L: 그러자 그 여자가 말했다. "내가 반드시 너와 함께 가겠다. 다만 네가 가는 길에서 영예가 네 것이 되지 않을 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 시스라를 한 여자의 손에 파실 것이기 때문이다." 그리고 드보라가 일어나 바락과 함께 게데스로 갔다.
ko.B: 드보라가 말했다. "내가 반드시 너와 함께 가겠다. 그러나 네가 가는 이 길에서 영예는 너에게 돌아가지 않을 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 시스라를 한 여자의 손에 넘기실 것이기 때문이다." 그리고 드보라는 바락과 함께 게데스로 떠났다.
ko.R: 드보라가 말했다. "그래, 내가 너와 함께 가겠다. 그러나 이렇게 가면 너는 영예를 얻지 못할 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 한 여자가 시스라를 이기게 하실 것이다." 그래서 드보라는 바락과 함께 게데스로 갔다.

pt.L: E ela disse: "Certamente irei com você; somente que a honra não será sua no caminho em que você vai, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} venderá Sísera na mão de uma mulher." E Débora se levantou e foi com Baraque a Quedes.
pt.B: "Com certeza irei com você", disse ela. "Mas, no caminho que você está tomando, a honra não será sua, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} entregará Sísera nas mãos de uma mulher." Então Débora se pôs a caminho com Baraque para Quedes.
pt.R: "Sim, eu vou com você", disse ela. "Mas, do jeito que você está fazendo, a honra não vai ser sua. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai deixar uma mulher derrotar Sísera." Então Débora foi com Baraque a Quedes.

am.L: እርሷም፦ «በእርግጥ ከአንተ ጋር እሄዳለሁ፤ ነገር ግን {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሲሣራን በሴት እጅ ይሸጠዋልና በምትሄድበት መንገድ ክብሩ ለአንተ አይሆንም።» አለች። ዲቦራም ተነሥታ ከባርቅ ጋር ወደ ቃዴስ ሄደች።
am.B: «በእርግጥ ከአንተ ጋር እሄዳለሁ» አለች፤ «ነገር ግን በምትሄድበት በዚህ መንገድ ክብሩ የአንተ አይሆንም፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሲሣራን በሴት እጅ አሳልፎ ይሰጠዋልና።» ስለዚህ ዲቦራ ተነሥታ ከባርቅ ጋር ወደ ቃዴስ ሄደች።
am.R: «አዎ፣ ከአንተ ጋር እሄዳለሁ» አለች፤ «ነገር ግን በዚህ በምትሄድበት መንገድ ክብሩን አታገኝም። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} አንዲት ሴት ሲሣራን ድል እንድታደርገው ያደርጋልና።» ስለዚህ ዲቦራ ከባርቅ ጋር ወደ ቃዴስ ሄደች።

decisions.choice: going I will go: I will surely go
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Deborah agrees at once and without doubt.

decisions.choice: your honor ... on the way you are going: the glory of the victory will not be yours on this undertaking
decisions.reason: "The way you are going" can mean the campaign he is setting out on, or the way he has chosen to act, with conditions. Either way, Barak will not have the honor of killing the enemy commander.

decisions.choice: into the hand of a woman: a woman will defeat Sisera
decisions.reason: A reader expects the woman to be Deborah, but the story will show that it is Jael (verses 17-22). The same verb "sell" from verse 2 is used: the LORD, who sold Israel to Jabin, now sells Jabin's commander.

decisions.choice: on the road you are taking / the way you are going
decisions.reason: Both renderings keep the Hebrew open: the phrase can mean the campaign itself or the way Barak has chosen to go about it.

decisions.choice: will let a woman defeat
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "sell into the hand of" in plain words.

records.literal_gloss: And summoned Barak Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and went up at his feet ten thousands man; and went up with him Deborah.

en.L: And Barak called out Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men went up at his feet; and Deborah went up with him.
en.B: Barak called out the men of Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men marched up behind him. Deborah went up with him too.
en.R: Barak called the men of Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men followed him. Deborah went with him too.

decisions.reason: The verb means to cry out, and in this form to call people together; it is used for raising troops (6:34-35).

decisions.reason: To go "at someone's feet" is to follow his lead (8:5; Exodus 11:8).

decisions.choice: the men of Zebulun and Naphtali
decisions.reason: The tribes are named, but it was their fighting men who were called. Balanced and Readable add "the men of".

records.literal_gloss: And Heber the Kenite [had] separated from Kain, from [the] sons of Hobab, father-in-law of Moses, and he pitched his tent as far as [the] great tree in Zaanannim, which [is] near Kedesh.

en.L: And Heber the Kenite had separated from Kain, from the sons of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the great tree in Zaanannim, which [is] near Kedesh.
en.B: Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far away as the great tree in Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
en.R: Now a man named Heber had moved away from the rest of his people, the Kenites. They were descended from Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses. Heber had set up his tent far to the north, by the big tree at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.

sw.L: Naye Heberi Mkeni alikuwa amejitenga na Kaini, na wana wa Hobabu, baba mkwe wa Musa, naye alikuwa amepiga hema lake mpaka kwenye mti mkubwa ulioko Zaananimu, [ulio] karibu na Kedeshi.

decisions.choice: an aside: background the reader needs for verse 17
decisions.reason: The sentence breaks off the story to explain how a Kenite family came to be living in the north, near the battlefield. Its verbs describe what had happened earlier.

decisions.choice: the Kenites, Kain, and Hobab
decisions.reason: The Kenites were a desert clan linked by marriage to Moses, who went with Israel into the land and settled in the south of Judah (1:16). "Kain" is the clan's ancestor's name, used for the whole clan (Numbers 24:21-22). Heber had left them and moved north.

decisions.choice: Hobab the father-in-law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word means a relative by marriage, usually a father-in-law, and 1:16 also calls Moses' father-in-law a Kenite. But Numbers 10:29 calls Hobab the son of Reuel, Moses' father-in-law, which would make Hobab Moses' brother-in-law. The word may cover either relationship, or the family may have had more than one name for its head.

decisions.choice: the great tree in Zaanannim
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text give a slightly different spelling of the place (Zaanaim), and the margin of the text tells readers to say "Zaanannim", the form found in Joshua 19:33, a place on Naphtali's border. The spoken form is followed. The "great tree" was a large oak or terebinth that served as a landmark; Joshua 19:33 may treat the two words together as one name.

decisions.choice: the Kenites
decisions.reason: Balanced names the clan by its usual name instead of the bare ancestor's name "Kain".

decisions.choice: far to the north
decisions.reason: The Kenites lived in the far south (1:16). Readable says where Heber had gone, which the Hebrew "as far as" implies.

decisions.choice: "Ca-in" at Literal; "người Kê-nít" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Kain is the clan name from which "Kenite" comes (m2); Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does, and the other levels say "the Kenites".

decisions.choice: Héber, o queneu; Caim (L), os queneus (B); Hobabe; o grande carvalho de Zaananim
decisions.reason: "Héber" is the Brazilian form of the name; "Hobabe" and "Zaananim" as Numbers 10:29 and Joshua 19:33 have them in Portuguese. Literal keeps the clan's ancestor's name (m2), which is the same as Cain's, as the English Literal keeps "Kain"; Balanced names the clan. "Carvalho" is the usual Portuguese word for such a great tree, as the English says "great tree"; Readable says "grande árvore".
